mercy_translation.text:
Who, then, accomplished these things? Who brought those who hated one another together into peace except the beloved Son of the Father, the common Savior of all, Jesus Christ, who in his love endured all things for our salvation?

For from long ago the peace brought about by him had been prophesied, as Scripture says: “They shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.”

And this is not unbelievable, since even now peoples whose customs are naturally fierce, while they still sacrifice to their idols, rage against one another and cannot endure to remain even for an hour without a sword.

But when they hear the teaching of Christ, immediately instead of wars they turn to agriculture; instead of arming their hands with swords, they stretch them out in prayer. And in general, instead of warring against one another, they arm themselves against the devil and demons, fighting them through self-control and the virtue of the soul.

This is a sign of the Savior's divinity: what human beings had been unable to learn from idols, they learned from him. And it is no small exposure of the weakness and nothingness of demons and idols. For the demons, knowing their own weakness, formerly stirred human beings to fight against one another so that, if they ceased from mutual conflict, they might not turn toward the struggle against demons.

Indeed, those who become disciples of Christ, no longer fighting against one another, array themselves against demons through their conduct and acts of virtue. They drive them away and mock their leader, the devil: in youth they practice self-control, in trials they endure, in hardships they persevere, when insulted they bear it, when deprived they regard it lightly; and, most remarkable of all, they even despise death and become martyrs of Christ.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The prophecy cited is Isaiah's vision of swords transformed into agricultural tools.
Athanasius frames Christian moral transformation as spiritual warfare rather than interpersonal violence.
